normative_summary: Authoritative Preview evaluates only the saved Template current.
An unsaved EditorSession cannot be authoritative Evaluation input.
A clean EditorSession may preview current directly.
A dirty EditorSession presents Save and Preview as the primary action.
Save and Preview performs a complete explicit save before starting an independent preview operation.
Preview starts only after save success and a READY snapshot from that save's authoritative recheck.
Save failure or confirmed INVALID save starts no preview.
The server stores no autosave, Patch, or EditorSession.
The client may store a DesignDSL working copy and minimal edit state as a device-local recovery draft.
Recovery draft content is restored, exported, or discarded only by explicit author action.
A recovery draft creates no revision and does not synchronize across devices.
Recovery drafts omit RootDocument, customValues, preview images, and Asset bytes by default.
Each EditorSession has at most one Template save or invalid-confirmation mutation in flight.
Authored mutations pause while a Template mutation is in flight.
Structure, property, and problem browsing remains available during the mutation pause.
Successful save rebuilds the entire baseline from server canonical DesignDSL, revision, and contentHash.
Failed save preserves the local working copy unchanged and releases the mutation pause.
v1 has no submitted-versus-working draft layers, post-response command replay, or background save queue.
Every save requires expectedRevision concurrency control.
Conflict recovery provides no three-way diff, automatic merge, or item-level selection.
Conflict recovery preserves the complete local DesignDSL and reports that remote current advanced.
Local overwrite requires one explicit author confirmation.
After confirmation the client reads latest revision and resubmits complete DesignDSL with it as expectedRevision under full validation.
Further drift before or during retry returns a new conflict and requires new confirmation.
Conflict overwrite is neither silent nor unconditional last-write-wins.
Invalid commit confirmation binds only a complete untruncated dependency ERROR set.
Any hard error or PROBLEM_LIMIT_REACHED forbids issuing or using invalid confirmation.
A forbidden confirmation attempt performs zero writes.
The author must reduce problems and revalidate until the complete confirmation set is visible.
Each Template has at most one recovery draft per device.
A recovery record stores base revision, base contentHash, complete DesignDSL working copy, minimal edit state, and updated time.
A successful local authored command replaces the recovery record after bounded debounce and retains no draft history.
Recovery clears on successful clean save, explicit discard, Template deletion, or age beyond seven days.
Browser quota reclamation may remove recovery earlier.
Local recovery is best-effort and not a durability promise.
A recovery draft whose base equals server current may restore directly as a dirty EditorSession on that current.
When current advanced, UI reports the changed baseline before allowing restoration of the complete local draft.
Restoration itself writes nothing and its later save uses normal conflict-overwrite confirmation.
The client never automatically adopts a local draft or overwrites server current.
Leaving a dirty EditorSession through editor navigation offers Save, Keep local draft and leave, and Cancel.
If save is unavailable or fails, Keep local draft and leave and Cancel remain available.
Browser close, refresh, and crash recovery relies only on best-effort beforeunload and Local recovery draft.
Reopening offers Restore, Export, and Discard and never auto-loads or submits recovery content.
Recovery records never store RootDocument, customValues, preview images, or Asset bytes.
An EditorSession has one Authoritative Preview result slot and one active preview operation.
Preview basis includes saved current, absence of local divergence, RootDocument or customValues sample, format, DPI, JPEG quality, and LayoutTrace choice.
Any DesignDSL edit, sample-input or parameter change, or current revision or readiness change immediately withdraws the image and requires a new preview.
Panel visibility and selection movement do not affect preview basis.
Starting a preview best-effort cancels the previous operation.
Starting a new preview immediately revokes the previous operation's display eligibility.
Author cancel immediately clears the preview result slot.
Cancel may lose to Engine seal.
A client generation guard discards every late success or failure from an old operation.
v1 has no preview history, parallel result slots, or automatic rerun.
Save and Preview consists of two sequential non-atomic operations.
Successful Template save permanently appends its revision.
Later preview cancel or runtime failure cannot roll back a successful save.
UI separately reports save success and preview failure or cancellation.
UI cannot present Save and Preview as one transaction or classify preview failure as save failure.
Historical restore of an ACTIVE Template can start only from a clean EditorSession.
Before restore, unsaved content must be saved, exported, or discarded.
Restore confirmation shows exact source and current revision, contentHash, and authoritative problems but no three-way or semantic diff.
Restore carries current expectedRevision and appends source DesignDSL as a new revision.
Restore may enter INVALID only through the existing complete dependency-error confirmation flow.
Further current drift makes restore zero-write and requires new confirmation.
A DELETED Template remains limited to read-only, export, or copying exact history into a new Template.
The editor has exactly three explicit mutually exclusive content modes.
Structured Editor requires complete client understanding of exact dslVersion, expressionProfile, NodeContractCatalog, and every closed wire member.
Structured Editor may project a valid canvas or a best-effort invalid canvas.
Raw Repair is used for illegal UTF-8 or JSON, duplicate keys, or other raw imports that cannot produce a trusted DesignDSL.
Raw Repair permits only repair, replacement, download, or discard of raw input.
Compatibility Read-only is used for complete input whose exact profile or wire is not understood by the client.
Compatibility Read-only permits only safe metadata viewing, export, or explicit migration.
No editor mode may partially reserialize content.
No editor mode may discard unknown members and save.
No editor mode may treat browser guesses as compatibility interpretation.
Raw Repair enters Structured Editor only after strict UTF-8 JSON, no duplicate keys, supported exact profile pair, and complete closed-model construction all succeed.
Before Raw Repair conversion, the UI exposes no structure tree, property inspector, best-effort Canvas, Template save, or Authoritative Preview.
Compatibility Read-only enters Structured Editor only after a contentHash-bound migration preview succeeds and the author accepts it.
The original compatibility content always remains exportable.
Migration never rewrites original compatibility content in place.
Structured continuous property, number, text, Expression, ValueSource, and direct-JSON edits may temporarily produce hard or dependency problems.
Supported imported content may begin in invalid state.
Each discrete create, copy, delete, move, reparent, or reorder command atomically generates and remaps every affected domain and target identity or reference.
A structural command is rejected in full with a locatable reason when identity, lexical reachability, ContentModel, placement, or reference-rewrite safety cannot be proved.
A rejected structural command leaves no partial local mutation.
The client cannot delegate repair guesses to the server.
Undo and redo are local structural-command history within one Canonical editor baseline.
Every undo or redo step restores a complete EditorSession working copy even through temporary invalid states.
Successful save, conflict overwrite, revision restore, and whole-Template copy or create adopt a new server canonical baseline and clear undo or redo.
Content across canonical baselines is restored only from immutable Template revision history and cannot replay old local commands.
Accepted import or migration preview writes nothing, clears prior undo or redo, and creates a complete dirty working draft anchored to the original baseline.
Only a later successful ordinary save creates the next canonical baseline for imported or migrated content.
Reordering a semantic array applies one permutation and atomically rewrites every affected numeric targetPropertyRef to follow the moved item.
Unsafe rewrite, out-of-bounds result, duplicate target, or ancestor-descendant overlap rejects the entire reorder.
v1 has no alternate keep-numeric-index reorder mode.
The editor cannot invent item identity for semantic arrays.
The editor provides one unified keyboard-accessible problem panel.
Problems are visibly separated into hard save blockers, confirmable dependency errors, and operation-only runtime or preview problems.
Stable problem code carries semantics and Chinese text is projected from code and message arguments.
Within authorization, each problem retains canonical pointer and relevant domain identity, target reference, or exact zero-based UTF-16 Expression span.
Raw business values and unauthorized child paths remain redacted.
Local lint binds to EditorSession content generation.
Server current reports bind to the read current revision and contentHash.
Save, import, and migration problems bind to submitted canonical content.
Preview problems bind to public renderOperationId and Authoritative Preview basis.
Any late report, validation, or preview result with mismatched basis or generation is discarded.
After explicit save or preview failure, focus moves to a problem summary containing total, category, and truncation state without changing Canvas or tree selection.
Navigation and focus to an entity, property, or source span occurs only when the author activates that problem.
Opening an ACTIVE Template first reads and verifies trusted canonical current and establishes the Canonical editor baseline.
Prior readiness and reports are not current conclusions and UI shows authoritative recheck in progress.
A supported exact model that passes the integrity gate may enter Structured Editor.
Structured Editor permits local editing and explicit save while current recheck runs.
Authoritative Preview stays disabled until current and closure recheck succeeds.
Only a new report bound to current revision and contentHash replaces checking state.
When remote current advances during a clean EditorSession, the client automatically adopts trusted canonical DesignDSL, revision, and contentHash.
Clean-current adoption clears undo or redo and withdraws preview.
Clean-current adoption reports the revision update non-blockingly.
Still-existing panel, expansion, and selection state may be preserved but is not content fact.
Remote content never overwrites a dirty EditorSession.
Remote advance marks a dirty canonical baseline stale while preserving the draft.
Saving a dirty stale baseline enters the normal conflict-overwrite flow.
Readiness and dependency events must match current.
STALE, INVALID, or a new recheck immediately withdraws preview.
A Template becoming DELETED immediately disables edit, save, and preview.
A DELETED Template exposes only read-only history, export, and copy capabilities.
Deletion does not automatically remove an unsaved working draft or Local recovery draft, which remain exportable.
Recovery and conflict overwrite cannot reactivate the deleted Template.
Import, accepted migration preview, and Local recovery share the dirty guard before replacing a working draft.
The dirty guard requires save, export, keeping current recovery while leaving, or explicit discard.
Accepted replacement becomes a complete dirty working draft and clears old undo or redo with zero server writes.
Only an ordinary later save appends a revision for replaced content.
Supported exact-pair invalid content enters Structured Editor best-effort mode and unconstructable content enters Raw Repair.
A complete exact wire not fully understood by the client enters Compatibility Read-only.
Importing an exact revision export first verifies exportVersion and canonical contentHash.
File templateId, revision, StaticSchemaRef, and contentHash show provenance only and grant no identity, authority, or target replacement.
Import into an existing Template preserves its permanent StaticSchemaRef.
For new Template creation, file StaticSchemaRef is only a prefilled suggestion requiring explicit author confirmation, authorization, and validation.
A bare DesignDSL import requires separate Schema selection.
Cross-scope TemplateRef and AssetRef are not automatically mapped, deep-copied, or authorization-preserved.
Every successful save rebuilds the baseline from a trusted canonical server response or GET.
Metadata trim, set sorting, or equivalent-decimal normalization produces only an expandable non-blocking category and count summary, not a complete diff.
Exact Expression source, Unicode, semantic array order, and every supported field must survive canonical resynchronization.
Response contentHash or integrity mismatch fails closed.
A contract-forbidden semantic change fails closed and cannot load suspect content into Structured Editor.
On canonical-response failure the client preserves an exportable local submission copy, reports compatibility failure, and rereads trusted current.
The client cannot present an already-committed server revision as rolled back.
The UI shows the variable-preview warning only when the complete Template closure declares Clock or Random Evaluation Capability.
Every new Authoritative Preview creates a new CapabilityState.
Browser drafts may show only visibly non-authoritative simulation or placeholders.
UI neither displays nor persists actual Clock or Random result, snapshot, nonce, call position, fingerprint, result digest, or internal recovery state.
Ctrl or Cmd plus S triggers explicit save.
Ctrl or Cmd plus Z and Ctrl or Cmd plus Shift plus Z trigger undo and redo, with Ctrl plus Y also triggering redo on Windows.
Delete or Backspace deletes only a deletable selection when tree or Canvas owns explicit focus and focus is outside text or editing controls.
A keyboard deletion is undoable.
Escape closes only temporary panel, menu, or dialog state and restores focus to its trigger.
Authoritative Preview and cancel have no global shortcut.
Invalid confirmation, conflict overwrite, restore, accepted import or migration, and Template or Asset deletion have no global shortcut.
Critical operations use named buttons and explicit confirmation.
Keyboard shortcuts do not execute during IME composition.
Supported desktop viewports target WCAG 2.2 AA.
The structure tree uses correct tree and roving-focus semantics.
Inspector, Binding, problems, history, import, and preview core flows work by keyboard alone.
Canvas selection has an equivalent entry in tree or problem panel.
Status, Binding, and severity never rely on color alone.
Every control has visible focus and an accessible name.
Progress and non-blocking changes use restrained polite live regions while blocking errors use a focused summary without duplicate announcements.
The editor follows reduced-motion preference.
At 200-percent zoom control panels remain scrollable and operable.
The two-dimensional Canvas may use necessary horizontal and vertical panning.
Below the desktop threshold, the unsupported-width state itself remains keyboard and screen-reader operable.
Unsupported narrow viewports cannot masquerade as an editable mobile UI.
No stage of a core keyboard workflow may create a keyboard trap.
Binding type-invalid and property-invalid states use distinct accessible text and state instead of one generic error.
A redacted or unavailable problem location remains understandable from authorized information and never fabricates a locator or placeholder.
Each control exposes stable accessible name, role, value, validation, expanded, and selected semantics when applicable.
Core workflows remain fully operable under platform-supported high-contrast settings.
Structured Editor enables save only when working draft and canonical baseline have a canonical semantic-content difference.
A clean UI cannot append a meaningless same-contentHash revision.
The domain API may still allow a controlled caller to explicitly save the same hash.
Dirty state uses complete exact-profile canonicalization or reliable complete command state since the canonical baseline.
Transport bytes, object order, and form-touched flags cannot determine dirty state.
A transport-unknown save enters Save reconciliation.
Save reconciliation preserves the authored-mutation lock, working draft, proposed contentHash, and Local recovery draft.
A timeout is not reported as success or failure and does not trigger blind resend.
Reconciliation first reads trusted current.
If current advanced beyond expectedRevision and equals proposed contentHash, the client adopts it and reports server confirmation without claiming request ownership.
If current still equals original expectedRevision, only an explicit author action may retry.
If current advanced with a different hash, reconciliation enters conflict overwrite.
If the target is DELETED, reconciliation enters read-only and export state.
Revision regression, integrity mismatch, and unexplained current state fail closed.
When trusted current is unreadable, Save reconciliation remains unknown.
Unknown reconciliation forbids new Template mutation, preview, and recovery-draft cleanup.
During unknown reconciliation the author may export the draft or leave after explicitly retaining recovery.
Reopening the Template resumes reconciliation before ordinary editing.
Only adoption of a trusted canonical baseline clears recovery and mutation lock and decides whether Save and Preview continues.
Create and copy with unknown transport result are not automatically retried because no duplicate-prevention command key exists.
The UI refreshes the Template directory and reports the create or copy result as unknown.
When a new object cannot be reliably correlated, the author checks the directory and sees a duplicate-risk warning before manually retrying.
v1 adds no private source lineage, client identity, or pseudo-idempotency key.
Conflict overwrite, invalid commit, revision restore, accepted migration, and deletion confirmations retain distinct exact semantics.
Distinct confirmations cannot collapse into a generic force-continue action.
After conflict overwrite confirmation, new authoritative validation independently issues any invalid-confirmation token for the new content and dependency snapshot.
Intermediate drift returns to its corresponding confirmation step and cannot reuse old confirmation.
A submitted Template save or confirmation mutation exposes no cancel operation.
The client cannot infer from a local cancel that the server did not commit.
Mode replacement, import, restore, and leave are blocked until mutation terminal state or explicit unknown reconciliation.
Forced browser close relies only on Local recovery draft.
Unknown state may leave with recovery but must reconcile first on the next open.
Authoritative Preview cancel remains independent best-effort Rendering control and does not imply save cancellation.
v1 Editor has no server autosave or Patch.
v1 Editor has no realtime collaboration or session lock.
v1 Editor has no automatic or three-way merge.
v1 Editor has no semantic diff.
v1 Editor has no unconditional last-write-wins.
v1 Editor has no preview history or parallel preview slots.
v1 Editor has no cross-device draft synchronization.
v1 Editor has no Workspace fixture.
v1 Editor has no fallback to old authoritative images.
v1 Editor cannot save a partial model.
v1 Editor has no generic force confirmation.
Ticket18 freezes product workflow, state, domain language, and later implementation and acceptance constraints only.
Ticket18 creates no Template or Asset API, database, EditorSession store, frontend product route, Evaluator or Renderer capability, or other product code.
Ticket19 must supply every named capacity value and freeze cross-language, cross-platform, security, and WCAG evidence levels.
